produced_findings.claim: `page()` returns one extra item per page (off-by-one slice end) `end = offset + page_size + 1` makes the slice `items[offset:offset + page_size + 1]`, which is `page_size + 1` elements whenever enough items remain. For `items=[1..10]`, `page_size=3`: page 1 returns `[1,2,3,4]` and page 2 returns `[4,5,6,7]`. The committed version, `items[offset : offset + page_size]`, returns exactly `page_size` items. The repository has no caller, test, or documentation that justifies the extra element. Every full page is larger than requested, and the last item of page N is repeated as the first item of page N+1. Consumers see duplicate records and wrong page sizes. Any client that treats a page of exactly `page_size` items as "more pages remain" is also misled.

Message-building step is duplicated across the email and sms branches The `sms` branch repeats `msg = format_message(user)` from the `email` branch at `app/notify.py:3`. The two branches differ only in the recipient (`user.email` vs `user.phone`) and the sender (`send_email` vs `send_sms`). Message construction now has two copies. If a channel needs different formatting, or `format_message` gains a parameter such as the channel, someone must change every branch. A missed branch would make the channels diverge. Each new channel adds another copy.

Shell command injection via `name` in `make_archive` `name` is interpolated directly into `cmd` (line 5) and executed with `shell=True` (line 6), so the shell interprets any metacharacters in it. For example, `make_archive("x; id #")` runs `tar -czf x; id #.tar.gz data/` and so also runs `id`. The previous list-form call passed `name` as a single argv element and never reached a shell. A repository search found no in-repo callers of `make_archive`, so where `name` comes from is not established here. Any caller that passes externally influenced input as `name` gives an attacker arbitrary command execution as the process user. A name containing a space, quote or `$` also breaks or changes the archive command even without malicious intent. The change adds this risk and has no functional benefit. `shell=True` with a single string hands the whole string to `/bin/sh -c`. Every `;`, `&&`, `|`, backtick, `$()` or newline in `name` therefore starts a new command. Quoting with `shlex.quote` would reduce the risk, but a list-form call avoids the shell entirely.
